root.name: King's Indian Defense: Kazakh Variation
root.moves: 1. d4 Nf6 2. c4 g6 3. Nc3 Bg7 4. e4 d6 5. Nf3 O-O 6. Be2 Na6

overview: Black puts the queen's knight on a6 before committing the pawn break, from where it can go to c7 or b4 and supports ...e5 or ...c5. After 7.O-O Black plays ...e5, ...c6 or ...c5 depending on White's set-up; 7.Bg5 is the other White try. The structures range from Mar del Plata-like locked centres to Benoni-style ones. White expands on the queenside while Black attacks on the kingside.

white_ideas.idea: Castle, play Be3 or Re1 and meet ...e5 with d5 or dxe5 to keep a central edge.
Expand on the queenside with c5 or a5 against the knight on a6.

black_ideas.idea: Support ...e5 with ...c6 and ...Nc7 and then attack with ...Nd7 or ...exd4.
Strike with ...c5 for a Benoni-style game with pressure on the d-file.

typical_structures.structure: King's Indian centre with c4/d4/e4 against d6/e5 or c5, often closing after d5.

character.notes: King's Indian play with the knight on a6 leads to unbalanced pawn structures and attacks on opposite wings.

structure.notes: After ...e5 and d5 the centre locks, though ...c5 lines can stay fluid.

level.notes: Choosing between ...e5, ...c5 and ...c6 and timing the attack takes understanding; theory is moderate.

sublines_that_differ.name: 7...c5
sublines_that_differ.how: A Benoni-style game with a half-open d-file.

character.reason: King's Indian structures lead to opposite-wing attacks where timing errors lose quickly.

structure.reason: Typical outcome is a locked centre after ...e5 and d5, with play on the wings.

level.reason: A sideline of the Orthodox with moderate theory but plans needing understanding.

plans.reason: Black's typical plan is a kingside pawn storm.
